🔧 Bike Fit Calculator

🏆 Rider & Bike

1. Rider Morphologies (User Inputs)

Rider InseamOverall leg extension axis from the saddle reference point down to the pedal spindle at Bottom Dead Center (BDC).
Torso LengthUpper-body vector line running along the spine from hip pivot (Greater Trochanter) to shoulder joint.
Arm LengthUpper arm vector line from the shoulder joint pivot dot to the elbow joint.
Forearm LengthForearm vector line from the elbow pivot dot resting on the pad to the hand/wrist grip center.
Static Acromion Width (Wstatic)Shoulder-width callout line in the upper-right anatomical legend diagram, referenced on the shoulder joint axis.
Elbow Flare Width (Welbow)Forearm/elbow orientation relative to the pad centerlines in the top-center inset.

2. Cockpit & Position Tuning

Aerodynamic AggressivenessOverall torso drop angle, head height, and pad-to-saddle drop differential on the TT rider.
Wrist Extension Toe-In (θtoe-in)Labeled in the Aero Cockpit Details inset, showing the extension's inward angle.
Aero Pad Center-to-Center Width (Wpad)Labeled on the vertical span between the arm pads in the top-center inset.
Aero Extension Grip Width (Wgrip)Labeled across the extension tips in the top-center inset, illustrating the frontal aerodynamic V-wedge.

3. Frame & Component Geometry

Frame StackVertical dimension axis extending from the Bottom Bracket (BB) center up to the top of the headtube/stem interface.
Frame ReachHorizontal dimension axis extending from the BB center forward to the headtube centerline.
Stem Length & Handlebar ReachHorizontal reach vectors running from the headtube axis through the stem to the drop/hood trough on the road setup.
Crank LengthLabeled directly at the crank arm and pedal axle interface on the road bike bottom bracket.

4. Biomechanical Targets & Joint Pivots

Joint Pivots (Red Dots)Precise rotation centers at the Hip (Greater Trochanter), Knee, Ankle, Shoulder, Elbow, and Wrist.
Knee Angle BDC (30°–40°)Labeled on the posterior arc at the knee joint when the crank arm is at Bottom Dead Center.
Saddle HeightLabeled along the seat tube / seatpost axis running from the BB center to the saddle midpoint reference line.
